system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: Kubernetes
G2: AWS/GCP
G3: LLM fine-tuning or LLMs in production
G4: computer vision
G5: completed PhD

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Translating 'Doktorandica (u tijeku)' as holding a PhD or adding 'Dr.'
T2: Inventing LLM/RAG production experience from the weekend demo
T3: Adding Kubernetes, AWS, MLOps platforms (Kubeflow, SageMaker) because ML ads list them
T4: Mistranslating employer or degree (Mag. ing. comp. is a master's degree)
T5: Writing the English output with Croatian section headings or leaving Croatian text untranslated
T6: Old Croatian cover letter is addressed to her current employer

# OUTPUT 1: CV
PETRA ZLATARIĆ-NOVOSEL
Machine Learning Engineer
Osijek, Croatia | petra.zlataric@example.com | +385 55 555 0606 | github.com/pzn-ml-example
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Machine Learning Engineer with 5+ years of experience in natural language processing (NLP) and
document classification. Experienced in taking work from research and prototypes through to
production models. PhD candidate researching natural language processing for Croatian.
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
ML Engineer | Slavonica Document AI d.o.o., Osijek | 03/2023–Present
• Developed an automated classification model for incoming documents (invoices, contracts and
administrative decisions) for public administration clients, achieving 94% accuracy across 23

• Fine-tuned BERTić and XLM-R transformer models for named entity recognition on Croatian

• Introduced MLflow for experiment tracking and model registry; deployed models as FastAPI

• Mentor two students during internships.

09/2021–02/2023

team.
• Analyzed customer complaint text using topic classification (TF-IDF and logistic regression, later
fastText).
• Created SQL reports using an Oracle data warehouse.
Research Project Assistant | Faculty of Applied Informatics, University of Drava |
10/2020–08/2021
• Built a corpus of Croatian legal texts and annotated the data; wrote scripts in Python.
EDUCATION
PhD studies in Computer Science | University of Drava | 2022–Present
Research topic: Named entity recognition in Croatian legal texts.
Master of Computer Engineering (Mag. ing. comp.) | University of Drava | 2020
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, scikit-learn, LightGBM, fastText, spaCy, pandas,

LANGUAGES
Croatian (native), English (C1), German (B2)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
PETRA ZLATARIĆ-NOVOSEL
petra.zlataric@example.com | +385 55 555 0606
Dear Hiring Manager,
I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role at Quillstone
Payments. I bring more than five years of experience in NLP and document classification,
including taking machine-learning work from research and prototypes into production. The
role’s focus on building and operating AI systems for customer support is a strong match for
my experience delivering language and classification models.
In my current role at Slavonica Document AI, I developed a document-classification model
that achieved 94% accuracy across 23 classes and fine-tuned BERTić and XLM-R for named
entity recognition on Croatian documents. I introduced MLflow experiment tracking and a
model registry, and deployed models as FastAPI services in Docker containers on Azure ML
and App Service. I also established production monitoring for data drift with weekly
reporting.
My earlier work includes classifying customer complaint topics using TF-IDF, logistic
regression and fastText, as well as developing churn-prediction models using gradient boosting
and LightGBM. This combination of text-focused machine learning, model serving and
production monitoring would allow me to contribute to Quillstone’s work on answering
merchant questions, routing tickets and supporting agents. I am particularly drawn to the
opportunity to take AI ideas from prototype to production in a team focused on reducing
friction for merchants.
I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to
Quillstone’s Customer Operations AI team. Thank you for your consideration.
Sincerely, PETRA ZLATARIĆ-NOVOSEL

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
